examples: You remember discussing a flaky migration test last week but not which session it was; type flaky migration in the projects search box and the conversation opens with its summary and last messages.
You close forty old sessions before a trip; their summaries are written one at a time in the background by the Spark and are searchable as they land.
how_to: Close, remove or sleep a session: its last messages and details are saved at once and a summary is queued.
Search from the projects page search box, or GET /api/v1/conversations/search?q=flux%20cap&project=carnivore (words match by prefix, best match first, matches are marked in the snippet).
Open one with GET /api/v1/conversations/{conversation_id or session_uuid}: the summary, the last messages, the files touched and its restore points.

Set automatic summaries on close, how many messages are kept, and pause or resume the queue in settings > sessions & agents > conversation index; the queue length and the time it will take are shown there.
Index conversations you already closed with python3 scripts/conversation_index/backfill.py (dry run by default; it prints how long the summary queue will take).
media_exempt: A search box and settings panel on pages whose screenshots are recaptured before the next version bump.
name: Conversation index
summary: closed conversations are kept in the database with an llm-written summary, their last messages and a full-text search over both.
where: The projects page search box (results open the session detail), the session detail's summary and last messages, and settings > sessions & agents > conversation index. API under /api/v1/conversations/*.
